title: PhysxSurfaceDeformableBodyAPI
summary: PhysX collision substepping for a surface deformable body, read on the prim carrying OmniPhysicsDeformableBodyAPI only when its simulation mesh is a surface (OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableSimAPI) and PhysxSurfaceDeformableBodyAPI is listed in its usd-schemas. Without the API, or with a column absent, both values are 0, not the schema fallback 1.
producer_scope: Published like any applied physics API: every declared attribute at its resolved value. USD population also lists the built-in PhysxBaseDeformableBodyAPI in usd-schemas. No column is rewritten or created by the producer.

columns.name: physxDeformableBody:collisionIterationMultiplier
columns.absent: 0, the descriptor default, not the schema fallback 1 (the legacy USD loader defaulted to 1). PhysX then reports 0 collision substeps for the body, but the GPU solver runs the scene-wide maximum over all surface bodies, which starts at 1, so the simulation matches 1.
columns.notes: Ignored for a volume body. The property update applies a change to a surface body only.

columns.name: physxDeformableBody:collisionPairUpdateFrequency
columns.absent: 0, the descriptor default, not the schema fallback 1 (the legacy USD loader defaulted to 1). With the TGS solver 0 makes PhysX update surface collision pairs adaptively, and because the GPU solver keeps one value per scene, a single surface body with 0 makes pair updates adaptive for every surface body in the scene. Under PGS the pairs are updated once per step regardless.
columns.notes: Ignored for a volume body. The property update applies a change to a surface body only. The runtime's body defaults seed 1, but the parsed value (0) always replaces that seed.

interactions.rule: Read only on a prim enumerated by OmniPhysicsDeformableBodyAPI that the ovstage walker accepts as a deformable body: a Mesh, TetMesh or BasisCurves, or an Xformable that is not a Gprim, with exactly one simulation mesh (OmniPhysicsVolumeDeformableSimAPI or OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableSimAPI) on the prim itself or an immediate child.
Read only when the body's simulation mesh carries this API (a surface body); a volume body ignores both columns.
USD applies PhysxBaseDeformableBodyAPI as a built-in of this API; the parser checks that name separately, so a hand-populated body lists both.
